universal_patterns.name: Immediate Human Face & Provocative Question Hook
universal_patterns.description: The video opens in frame 0.0s with a human face looking directly into the lens, delivering a provocative pain or curiosity statement within the first 2.5 seconds.
universal_patterns.editorial_intent: Stop user feed scrolling, establish instant human connection and provoke immediate curiosity or self-identification.
universal_patterns.visual_response: Medium close-up of presenter looking straight at camera with rapid punch-in or cut within 2.5s.
universal_patterns.technique: Hard cut opening, kinetic bold title, immediate voice start (no intro bumper or logo).
universal_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Start video at t=0 with presenter face or property hero punch, with voice starting within 0.3s and first visual interrupt within 3.0s.
universal_patterns.caveats: REF_03 opened with an aerial context view before showing presenter, indicating scenic real estate can also hook with stunning drone visuals.

universal_patterns.name: Literal Semantic Materialization on Key Noun Mention
universal_patterns.description: The moment a specific physical space, feature, or tangible benefit is spoken (e.g. "cozinha", "bife", "varanda gourmet", "lote", "piscina"), the image cuts directly to that exact visual.
universal_patterns.observed_trigger: Presenter voice uttering physical feature, appliance, or room noun.
universal_patterns.editorial_intent: Validate spoken claim instantly with visual proof, creating high cognitive coherence.
universal_patterns.visual_response: Cut from presenter to high-quality B-roll or render of the spoken object.
universal_patterns.technique: Synchronous cut (aligned within ±100ms of the stressed noun).
example_shots: REF_01: SHOT_10 (fala sobre funcionária/área de serviço)
REF_01: SHOT_13 (fala sobre freezer vertical / despensa)
REF_05: SHOT_04-12 (fala sobre 109m², varanda gourmet conectada)
universal_patterns.hypothesized_rule: When script contains a high-value physical feature, trigger an immediate B-roll / photo cutaway lasting 1.5s to 3.5s.
universal_patterns.caveats: Do not cut away if the presenter is in the middle of a high-emotion personal epiphany.

universal_patterns.name: Syntactic Phrase Boundary Cut (Breath / Clause Cut)
universal_patterns.description: Cuts strictly align with the natural pause between clauses, comma breaks, or sentence completions, avoiding cutting mid-syllable.
universal_patterns.observed_trigger: Natural syntactic pause, comma, or end of sentence in speech transcript.
universal_patterns.editorial_intent: Maintain fluent acoustic cadence and prevent visual-audio dissonance.
universal_patterns.visual_response: Hard cut or transition placed cleanly during the millisecond gap between words.
example_shots: Across 92% of all 133 shots in dataset
universal_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Always align shot boundaries to speech pause points (inter-word gaps > 80ms) rather than arbitrary time intervals.
universal_patterns.caveats: If speech is continuous without pauses for 7+ seconds, a punch-in is preferable to an abrupt cut.

universal_patterns.name: Numerical Anchor Cut (Price, Area, Date)
universal_patterns.description: Speaking a quantifiable metric (e.g. "109 m²", "600 lotes", "300 mil", "2 suítes") triggers an immediate cut or graphics pop.
universal_patterns.observed_trigger: Speech transcript contains numeral, monetary value, or unit of measurement.
universal_patterns.editorial_intent: Anchor high-value factual data in visual memory.
universal_patterns.visual_response: Cut to full card, badge overlay, or architectural render showing the metric.
universal_patterns.technique: Graphic lower-third pop or full-screen card synchronized to number.
universal_patterns.hypothesized_rule: When price, area or key numbers are voiced, display matching on-screen typography or cut to relevant asset.
universal_patterns.caveats: Do not overload screen with more than one primary metric at a time.

universal_patterns.name: Presenter-to-B-roll Handoff and Semantic Return Loop
universal_patterns.description: Presenter introduces a topic, camera cuts to B-roll for 2 to 5 seconds to showcase it, and then camera cuts back to presenter for the emotional conclusion or next transition.
universal_patterns.observed_trigger: Transition from general premise to tangible evidence and back to reflection.
universal_patterns.editorial_intent: Create a rhythmic breathing cycle between human authority (face) and property proof (scenery).
universal_patterns.technique: A-roll / B-roll alternating loop with 100% return rate.
universal_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Limit isolated B-roll chains to 2-4 shots before returning to presenter to maintain personal connection.
universal_patterns.caveats: In pure property tours (REF_05), B-roll chains can extend to 10+ shots with presenter acting as voiceover.

universal_patterns.name: Dynamic Acceleration Curve (Hook Fast -> Body Steady -> CTA Punchy)
universal_patterns.description: Shot pacing accelerates in the opening hook (avg 1.8s/shot), stabilizes in the narrative body (avg 3.2s/shot), and tightens during the final call to action (avg 2.1s/shot).
universal_patterns.observed_trigger: Progression across narrative phases of the script.
universal_patterns.editorial_intent: Hook attention quickly, allow deep comprehension during explanation, and drive urgency during closing conversion.
universal_patterns.visual_response: Pacing adapts dynamically from 30+ cuts/min (start) to 18 cuts/min (body) to 25 cuts/min (CTA).
universal_patterns.technique: Variable cut duration according to narrative section.
universal_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Structure shot durations with a 3-tier pacing curve: Hook (< 2.2s), Body (2.5s - 4.5s), CTA (< 2.5s).
universal_patterns.caveats: Pure contemplative walkthroughs (REF_05) maintain a steadier rhythm throughout.

universal_patterns.name: High-Cadence Pattern Interruption (Every 2.5s - 4.0s)
universal_patterns.description: To sustain audience retention on short-form feeds, a noticeable sensory change (cut, scale punch, text pop, sound effect, or b-roll switch) occurs at least once every 3.4 seconds on average.
universal_patterns.observed_trigger: Continuous playback time reaching 3.0 - 4.0s without visual change.
universal_patterns.editorial_intent: Prevent habituation, reset viewer attention span and eliminate visual stagnation.
universal_patterns.visual_response: Trigger cut, zoom, graphic badge, or sound marker.
universal_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Never allow more than 4.5s of identical visual framing without triggering a pattern interrupt.
universal_patterns.caveats: Interrupt intensity must match brand archetype (subtle punch for luxury vs bold kinetic graphics for sales pitch).

universal_patterns.name: Kinetic Subtitles with Highlight Color on High-Value Words
universal_patterns.description: Subtitles are rendered centered in the bottom/middle safe zone, dynamically highlighting emphasized words (numbers, adjectives, verbs) in high-contrast yellow (#FFD700) or green (#00E676).
universal_patterns.editorial_intent: Guide reading eye, synchronize visual-auditory processing and emphasize key selling points.
universal_patterns.visual_response: 1 to 3 words displayed per beat, with keyword highlighted in accent color.
example_shots: Observed across 100% of reference videos in dataset
universal_patterns.hypothesized_rule: All speech tracks must have synchronized captions with bold sans-serif font and keyword color highlights.
universal_patterns.caveats: Position captions safely above platform UI controls (bottom 250px margin).

universal_patterns.name: Hard Cut Dominance with Motivated Camera Motion Cuts
universal_patterns.description: Over 88% of all transitions are clean hard cuts. Digital wipes or zooms are reserved strictly for major section breaks or dramatic hooks.
universal_patterns.editorial_intent: Maintain cinematic clarity, avoid tacky amateur transitions, and maximize editorial speed.
universal_patterns.visual_response: Instant frame switch on audio pause boundary.
universal_patterns.technique: Direct hard cut (0 frames transition duration).
example_shots: Present in 118 out of 133 total shots (88.7%)
universal_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Default to hard cuts for all internal shot transitions; use motion blur or whip pans only for chapter resets.
universal_patterns.caveats: Whip pans are only motivated when camera is already panning in that direction.

universal_patterns.name: Presenter Re-Anchoring & Direct Physical Gesture to Platform CTA Button
universal_patterns.description: In the final 5-8 seconds, the video returns to the presenter looking straight at camera, physically pointing downward towards the screen button ("Clica no botão aqui embaixo / no link da bio").
universal_patterns.observed_trigger: Closing call to action in script.
universal_patterns.editorial_intent: Remove friction, guide physical user touch, and establish personal closing accountability.
universal_patterns.visual_response: Presenter medium shot with downward hand gesture + animated arrow or button overlay.
universal_patterns.technique: Direct-to-camera eye contact + downward pointing gesture + verbal CTA.
example_shots: REF_01: SHOT_24-25 ("agora só depende de você")
REF_02: SHOT_36-37 ("liberada no botão de saiba mais")
REF_03: SHOT_26-28 ("só apertar no botão que tem aqui embaixo")
REF_04: SHOT_20-21 ("aperta no botão aqui abaixo, realiza seu cadastro")
REF_05: SHOT_21-22 ("só você clicar no link da bio ou entrar em contato")
universal_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Always conclude with presenter on camera looking at lens, delivering clear action guidance with downward spatial reference.
universal_patterns.caveats: Ensure presenter pointing aligns with the actual button placement of the deployment platform (Feed vs Stories vs Reels).

frequent_patterns.name: Immediate Visual Micro-Interrupts in Hook Window
frequent_patterns.description: During the first 5.0 seconds of the video, at least 2 to 4 rapid cuts or punch-ins occur to establish a fast perceptual rhythm.
frequent_patterns.editorial_intent: Prevent early drop-off and create high cognitive engagement.
frequent_patterns.visual_response: Series of micro-shots (0.25s to 1.5s) altering zoom scale or angle.
frequent_patterns.technique: Digital punch-in (scale 1.15x - 1.25x) or rapid b-roll tease.
frequent_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Inject at least 2 visual scale or angle disruptions in the first 4.0 seconds of speech.
frequent_patterns.caveats: Excessive micro-cuts can feel jarring in slow luxury property walkthroughs.

frequent_patterns.name: Conceptual Metaphor Cutaway for Abstract Pain or Proof
frequent_patterns.description: When the presenter discusses abstract pain points or achievements (e.g., "sofrendo", "bagunça", "30 milhões de views", "sem banco"), the video cuts to a metaphorical b-roll, meme, or graphic proof.
frequent_patterns.observed_trigger: Speech describing emotional frustration, numerical authority, or administrative barrier.
frequent_patterns.editorial_intent: Make intangible concepts visceral and emotionally charged.
frequent_patterns.visual_response: Cut to symbolic b-roll (dirty sink, smoking steak, dashboard screenshot, red objection icon).
example_shots: REF_04: SHOT_13-14 (cartela sem banco / sem comprovação)
frequent_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Pair abstract pain points with symbolic illustrative footage or graphic proof cards.
frequent_patterns.caveats: Must remain tasteful; real estate requires balancing tension with aspirational elegance.

frequent_patterns.name: Digital Scale Punch-In for Continuous Monologue
frequent_patterns.description: When the presenter continues talking for longer than 3.5 seconds on the same idea, the editor switches between Medium Shot (1.0x) and Close-Up (1.2x crop) without changing the background.
frequent_patterns.observed_trigger: Presenter speaking continuously for > 3.5s without cutaway to B-roll.
frequent_patterns.editorial_intent: Simulate a two-camera studio setup, maintain visual dynamism and emphasize important sentences.
frequent_patterns.visual_response: Instant change from Medium Shot to Close-Up (punch-in) or vice-versa.
frequent_patterns.technique: 2D Scale Transform (100% -> 120%) centered on presenter eyes.
frequent_patterns.hypothesized_rule: If presenter stays on screen for > 4.0s, apply a scale punch-in (1.18x) on the next emphatic word.
frequent_patterns.caveats: Source video must have sufficient resolution (e.g. 1080p/4K) to avoid digital blur.

frequent_patterns.name: Dynamic Motion B-roll (Slow Pan / Push-In / Drone)
frequent_patterns.description: B-roll footage is never completely static; it always features subtle camera motion (gimbal push-in, slow pan, or drone flight) to maintain kinetic energy.
frequent_patterns.observed_trigger: Displaying architectural space, room, or external landscape.
frequent_patterns.editorial_intent: Convey depth, luxury, and three-dimensional spatial understanding.
frequent_patterns.visual_response: Smooth forward push-in, lateral slider pan, or descending drone shot.
frequent_patterns.hypothesized_rule: When selecting property video segments or photos, prioritize footage with forward/lateral movement or apply slow digital Ken Burns push (1.05x).
frequent_patterns.caveats: Motion must be smooth; erratic handheld shaking degrades perceived property value.

frequent_patterns.name: Macro Detail / Texture Cutaways for Premium Quality
frequent_patterns.description: Brief insertion of close-up detail shots (fixtures, marble, barbecue grill, glass balcony railing) alongside wide room shots.
frequent_patterns.observed_trigger: Speech highlighting finish quality, decoration, or premium materials.
frequent_patterns.editorial_intent: Highlight high-end craftsmanship and tactile luxury.
frequent_patterns.visual_response: Tight close-up shot (1.0s - 2.2s) showing texture or architectural detail.
frequent_patterns.technique: Fast cutaway inserted between wider room shots.
frequent_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Pair wide room establishing shots with tight detail inserts when script mentions high-end finishes.
frequent_patterns.caveats: Requires rich b-roll library with macro coverage.

frequent_patterns.name: Persistent Top Headline Banner for Silent Feed Scrollers
frequent_patterns.description: A permanent high-contrast rectangular banner is placed at the top of the frame (above safe zones), stating the main offer or location throughout the entire video.
frequent_patterns.observed_trigger: Real estate promotional video targeting social media feed users.
frequent_patterns.editorial_intent: Provide instantaneous context to muted/silent viewers in the first 0.5s of scrolling.
frequent_patterns.visual_response: Fixed top badge with bold typography ("SEU LOTE EM GUARAPARI", "PRÉ-LANÇAMENTO JOCKEY").
frequent_patterns.technique: Static overlay positioned in safe top margin (y: 8-15%).
frequent_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Optionally enable a persistent top headline banner for feed ads to maximize instant thematic recognition.
frequent_patterns.caveats: Not used in personal organic storytelling (REF_01, REF_02) where it might feel too commercial.

frequent_patterns.name: Lower-Third Room / Feature Identifier Badge
frequent_patterns.description: When showing an interior space or apartment amenity, an elegant pill badge or lower-third card appears in the lower-left corner indicating the room name and key spec.
frequent_patterns.observed_trigger: Transition to new room or property feature.
frequent_patterns.editorial_intent: Orient the viewer spatially and reinforce architectural value.
frequent_patterns.technique: Subtle lower-third slide-in with 2.5s on-screen duration.
frequent_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Display room title badge during the first 2.0s of entering any new property room b-roll.
frequent_patterns.caveats: Must avoid colliding with dynamic captions.

frequent_patterns.name: Acoustic Punch Markers on Visual Transitions
frequent_patterns.description: Cuts, punch-ins, and graphic pop-ups are accompanied by subtle acoustic markers (whoosh, hit, bass drop, paper slide) tightly ducked under the voice track.
frequent_patterns.observed_trigger: Visual cut, punch-in, or text appearance.
frequent_patterns.editorial_intent: Reinforce visual transition with auditory feedback, increasing perceived production value.
frequent_patterns.visual_response: Visual change synchronized with audio transient SFX.
frequent_patterns.hypothesized_rule: Pair major visual transitions and price graphics with subtle acoustic accent SFX.
frequent_patterns.caveats: SFX must never overpower voice clarity; keep SFX at -14dB to -18dB relative to dialogue.

editorial_tensions.dimension: Ritmo de Corte: Hiper-Acelerado vs Contemplativo Imersivo

archetype_a.name: High-Frequency Conversion Pitch (Ex: REF_02)
archetype_a.characteristics: 35.1 cortes/min, shots médios de 1.7s, múltiplos micro-cortes e memes para retenção agressiva.
archetype_a.context_fit: Topo de funil, anúncios curtos de tráfego pago, público jovem / atenção dispersa.

archetype_b.name: Cinematic Property Walkthrough (Ex: REF_05)
archetype_b.characteristics: 19.5 cortes/min, shots médios de 3.1s, movimentos fluidos de gimbal, valorização estética dos ambientes.
archetype_b.context_fit: Imóveis de alto padrão, compradores qualificados, foco em apreciação de planta e acabamentos.

editorial_tensions.implication_for_engine: O Video Engine não pode ter um ritmo fixo monolítico. Deve suportar perfis editoriais selecionáveis (ex: "High-Pace Conversion" vs "Cinematic Showcase").

editorial_tensions.dimension: Presença do Apresentador: Protagonista Absoluto vs Voz Guia do Imóvel

archetype_a.name: Presenter-Dominant Authority (Ex: REF_01, REF_02, REF_04)
archetype_a.characteristics: Apresentador visível entre 86% e 100% do tempo. O imóvel aparece como cutaway pontual ou apoio.
archetype_a.context_fit: Venda de autoridade, persuasão direta, quebra de objeções complexas, storytelling de dor.

archetype_b.name: Property-Dominant Tour (Ex: REF_05, REF_03)
archetype_b.characteristics: Imóvel/B-roll visível entre 58% e 91% do tempo. Apresentador abre, ancora e fecha o vídeo.
archetype_b.context_fit: Apresentação detalhada de produto, quando o imóvel é a estrela indiscutível da compra.

editorial_tensions.implication_for_engine: O Creative Director deve equilibrar o ratio Presenter/B-roll conforme o objetivo da peça (Autoridade vs Demonstração de Imóvel).

editorial_tensions.dimension: Embalagem Gráfica: Banner Fixo Comercial vs Visual Clean Orgânico

archetype_a.name: Commercial Graphic Wrapper (Ex: REF_03, REF_04)
archetype_a.characteristics: Headline banner fixo no topo, badges de preço e parcelas permanentes.
archetype_a.context_fit: Anúncios diretos de lançamento e venda de lotes para tráfego frio.

archetype_b.name: Organic Native Video (Ex: REF_01, REF_02, REF_05)
archetype_b.characteristics: Tela limpa, apenas legendas dinâmicas centrais, sem molduras comerciais visíveis.
archetype_b.context_fit: Conteúdo orgânico de Reels, narrativas emocionais e tours sofisticados.

editorial_tensions.implication_for_engine: O motor gráfico deve tratar headers e badges como camadas modulares ativáveis sob demanda.
